To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a map of bull seminal proteins has been established, and some polypeptides have been identified.
we have developed a reference map of bull seminal proteins that could be useful in studying protein pattern changes in pathological situations.

we have developed a two‐dimensional gel electrophoreses map of bull seminal proteins, that we have identified the major proteins already known to be in bull semen, that we have found proteins not previously reported in male reproductive fluids and that we have found similarities between some of our proteins and proteins found in other species.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of proteins present in the seminal plasma of bulls, with the characterization of their structure, with the study of their expression in different physiological conditions, and with their possible involvement in the fertilization process.
establishing a map of seminal plasma polypeptides, which could be useful in studying protein pattern changes in relation to physiological or pathological events.
establishing the reference two‐dimensional gel map of proteins in seminal plasma, and to identify the polypeptides present in this complex mixture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bull seminal plasma proteome is very similar to the bovine milk proteome, and that both are more similar to the proteome of human milk than to the human seminal plasma proteome.
the present map of bull seminal vesicle proteins represents the first attempt to describe the proteome of a male reproductive tissue.

the present work has provided a reference map of bull seminal proteins, that will be useful for future investigations on bull fertility and infertility, on the physiology and pathology of the male genital apparatus and on the physiology of the female reproductive tract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a reference map of seminal proteins, that we have identified the proteins present in the spots of this map and that we have found some proteins not previously described.
the map is useful in relating protein changes to physiopatological events.
we have been able to identify 24 spots, 12 of which were not yet reported in the literature, and we have established a map of seminal plasma polypeptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two‐dimensional gel electrophoreses of bull semen is a useful technique to detect the presence or absence of proteins in semen.
we have developed a reference map of seminal fluid proteins that will be very useful in future studies to understand the physiology of male reproduction.
a reference map of bull seminal proteins can be used to identify proteins whose expression levels may change under physiological and pathological conditions.
